the formation of cross-links in bone collagen is a two-stage process, the first stage being the formation of precursors and the second the formation of crosslinks.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to show that the time lag between the maximal formation of precursors and that of cross-links of bone collagens in a cell culture model of osteoblastic cells is about one week, suggesting that there is a minimum essential accumulation of the collagen molecules for the transition from precursors to cross-links.

the collagen cross-linking is an essential step in bone formation and the cross-links of bone are not formed simultaneously with the synthesis of bone collagen but rather at a later stage of the bone formation process.
the time-dependent change of cross-link formation is a key factor that determines the quality and quantity of bone collagen.
